thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired (P1) -> svc-discovery-coredns-high-errors in us-west-2a. Auto-triage: service-discovery/lookup-timeout > 30s, impact: internal svc SRV resolution failures. Paging oncall-sre.
alex: I'm on it. Seeing spike in CoreDNS 5xx around 2034567850 in our observability. p99 DNS latency jumped from 8ms -> 420ms. Reproduced SRV lookup timeouts against coredns pods.
meera: @alex can you dump coredns pods + logs? I can start mitigation if it looks like overloaded peers.
alex: running: ```kubectl get pods -n discovery -l app=coredns -o wide``` Result: 5 pods, 3 in us-west-2a, 2 in us-west-2b. CPU on the 3 in 2a at ~95%, rest fine. Logs show repeated: `ERRO plugin/srv: lookup "_service._tcp.internal.svc" failed: context deadline exceeded` and `backpressure: active requests limit reached`.
jordan: Looks like cross-AZ routing causing request skew to 2a. Is there a control plane-change or scaling event? I don't see recent deploys in the last hour.
samir: Checked infra - there was a partial network degradation between us-west-2a and the peering mesh for ~7m starting 2034567800. BGP flaps reported by cloud provider, but core infra nodes remained healthy. That could increase retransmits and connection churn, amplifying DNS load on local pods.
alex: Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily route discovery traffic away from 2a to 2b (traffic-shift), 2) horizontally scale coredns in 2a and increase limit, 3) switch SRV resolver fallback to Consul cluster for critical services until stable. Rolling steps below.
meera: +1. I'm going to trigger a service mesh route override for service-discovery to prefer us-west-2b endpoints. On it.
meera: execute: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking/v1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: svc-discovery-pref-2b
  namespace: discovery
spec:
  host: svc-discovery.internal.svc.cluster.local
  trafficPolicy:
    loadBalancer:
      simple: LEAST_CONN
EOF
``` applied. Traffic shift should gradually move new lookups to 2b.
alex: Scaling coredns in 2a: ```kubectl scale deployment/coredns -n discovery --replicas=8 --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2a``` Patch applied; pods pending but will come up. Also bump coredns env `WORKER_LIMIT=200` on those pods.
jordan: I'm updating SRV client fallback config in runtime-config for critical internal services (auth, metadata): set SERVICE_DISCOVERY_FAILOVER=consul. After config change service rollouts will use consul for SRV lookups if coredns returns timeout.
samir: I see reduction in error-rate after mesh override started ~30s ago. Internal synthetic check for SRV -> passed from 2b. 5xx rate for internal API is down from 5.1% -> 1.2%.
oncall-sre: Taking over this incident. alex/meera, handoff notes: traffic shifted, coredns scaled to 8 in 2a, SRV clients updated to consul fallback. I'll monitor and coordinate with cloud provider for the peering BGP noise. PagerDuty: escalation paused; team still assigned.
alex: Quick check: still seeing some backlog in 2a pods logs with `backpressure: drop` but new requests mostly landing in 2b. We'll keep scaling until pods stabilize.
meera: Can we add a temporary TTL increase for service SRV records to reduce lookup volume? Suggest from 30s -> 300s for critical services.
oncall-sre: Approved. Patching zone config to TTL=300 for auth/metadata. ```curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-dns/control/zones/svc -d '{"ttl":300,"services":["auth","metadata"]}'``` Applied.
jordan: Running synthetic full stack check across regions. Results: us-west-2b OK, us-east latency normal. us-west-2a showing intermittent failures for cross-AZ queries but internal pod-local queries OK.
samir: Cloud provider says BGP flap mitigations are in progress; they estimate full convergence in ~10-15m. We'll plan keep consul fallback until they confirm stable for 30m.
alex: Current customer impact: internal control-plane RPCs to auth/metadata had ~3-6% failure rate for customers on us-west-2a during the window; external customer-facing APIs used cached tokens so public impact minimal. Logged affected customers and notified CS for heads-up.
meera: Creating temporary dashboard for this incident: dns-srv-errors, coredns-pod-cpu, coredns-restarts, svc-fallback-rate. Pinning it to incident channel.
oncall-sre: Noted. Steps for post-incident: 1) validate provider peering fix, 2) revert SRV TTL and consul fallbacks after 1h of stability, 3) run load test for SRV churn, 4) run postmortem. Assigning alex/jordan to draft postmortem.
alex: Patch for runbook: add explicit failover path to prefer cross-az healthy endpoints and consul fallback flag. Also add autoscaling rules for coredns based on srv-lookup QPS and backlog.
meera: Observability: synthetic SRV check now every 10s, alert threshold lowered to p95>100ms for quicker detection.
oncall-sre: Cloud provider confirmed BGP flaps resolved at 2034568380. We're in monitoring window. Last errors trending to 0.
alex: Confirming final numbers: incident start 2034567800, mitigation started 2034567890, provider resolved 2034568380, incident resolved + monitors quiet at 2034568410. Moving to post-incident.
samir: Noted. Will open follow-up ticket for infra to examine peering resiliency and consider multi-AZ egress paths for discovery traffic.
oncall-sre: Thanks team. If no objections, I'll close the active incident in 30m after stability window. :thumbsup:
meera: :thumbsup:
jordan: :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks all.
